Topic: Unveiling the Beauty of Conic Sections: The Dandelin Spheres

Target audience: High school geometry or early university mathematics students

Section: section_1 — Prerequisites: The Plane-Cone Intersection

Lecture lines:
A double-napped cone is our starting shape.
A plane slices the cone at various angles.
Different angles create circles, ellipses, parabolas, hyperbolas.

Planned animations:
Display a cone and a plane on a black background (#000000).
Highlight intersection points as the plane cuts the cone.
Change color to #FF5733 to emphasize the conic section.

Section: section_2 — Introducing Dandelin Spheres

Lecture lines:
Meet the Dandelin Spheres, a geometric bridge.
They fit perfectly inside the cone's interior.
They are tangent to both cone and plane.

Planned animations:
Display a sphere inside the cone touching the plane.
Show a second sphere on the opposite side of the cone.
Highlight the points of tangency in #33FF57.

Section: section_3 — Connecting the Dots: The Ellipse Proof

Lecture lines:
Tangency points on the plane become the foci.
Distance sum to foci is constant for ellipses.
This length equals the distance between circles of tangency.

Planned animations:
Draw an ellipse formed by the intersection.
Add two points representing the foci derived from spheres.
Use lines in #33A1FF to connect points to foci.

Section: section_4 — Generalization and Conclusion

Lecture lines:
Parabolas and hyperbolas also use this tangency principle.
Shifting the plane morphs the resulting conic section.
Tangency remains the key to all conic behavior.

Planned animations:
Show the plane tilting to create parabola and hyperbola.
Highlight how sphere tangency generalizes across all conic sections.
Fade all elements to #FFFFFF for a clear conclusion.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(ThreeDScene, TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Parabolas and hyperbolas also use this tangency principle.",
            "Shifting the plane morphs the resulting conic section.",
            "Tangency remains the key to all conic behavior."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Generalization and Conclusion", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define visual elements

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

            "Parabolas and hyperbolas also use this tangency principle.",

        self.place_in_area(plane_icon, "B2", "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_in_area(sphere_icon, "D2", "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Rotate(plane_icon, angle=PI/4, about_point=self.grid["B3"]))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(sphere_icon.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(FadeToColor(VGroup(plane_icon, sphere_icon), WHITE))
        self.wait(2)
